question.:question/problem:
Consider the following system of equations.

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}3x+2y &=-3 \\ -6x-4y &=6,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

which of the following statements are true?

I. The system is consistent independent

II. The system is consistent dependent

III. The system has no solution
question.:question/worked-solution:
To classify the system, we first need to find the solution to the system. The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}3 & 2 & -3 \\ -6 & -4 & 6\end{array}\right].
$$

Using the method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}3 & 2 & -3 \\ -6 & -4 & 6\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}3 & 2 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}3x+2y &=-3 \\ 0x+0y &=0.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Since any numbers $x$ and $y$ form a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of just a single equation:

$$
3x+2y=-3
$$

The basic variable is $x,$ and we have a free variable $y.$ That means we need to find $x$ in terms of $y.$ 

Therefore, since there are infinitely many solutions, we conclude that the system is *consistent dependent*.

As a result, only statement II is true.

question.:question/problem:
Consider the following system of equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-4x+3y &=-6 \\ -2x-2y &=2 \\ 2x-5y &=8.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Which of the following statements are true?

Select all that apply.
question.:question/worked-solution:
To classify the system, we first try to find its solution. The augmented matrix for this system is 

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}-4 & 3 & -6 \\ -2 & -2 & 2 \\ 2 & -5 & 8\end{array}\right].
$$

Using the method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}-4 & 3 & -6 \\ -2 & -2 & 2 \\ 2 & -5 & 8\end{array}\right] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}-2 & -2 & 2 \\ -4 & 3 & -6 \\ 2 & -5 & 8\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}-2 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 7 & -10 \\ 2 & -5 & 8\end{array}\right] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}-2 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 7 & -10 \\ 0 & -7 & 10\end{array}\right] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}-2 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 7 & -10 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

 

Since any numbers $x$ and $y$ are solutions to the third equation $0x+0y=0$, we can remove this equation from the system. So, the corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-2x-2y &=2 \\ 7y &=-10.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

From the second equation, we get $y=-\frac{10}{7}.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we get

$$
-2x-2\left(-\frac{10}{7}\right)=2\,⟹\,x=\frac{3}{7}.
$$

 
So, we conclude that the system is consistent independent. 

As a result, only statement “The system is consistent independent” is true.

question.:question/problem:
Consider the following system of equations.

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-4x-6y-2z &=10 \\ -6x-9y-3z &=15\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Which of the following statements are true?

Select all that apply.
question.:question/worked-solution:
To classify the system, we first need to find its solution. The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-4 & -6 & -2 & 10 \\ -6 & -9 & -3 & 15\end{array}\right].
$$

Using the method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-4 & -6 & -2 & 10 \\ -6 & -9 & -3 & 15\end{array}\right] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-2 & -3 & -1 & 5 \\ -6 & -9 & -3 & 15\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-2 & -3 & -1 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variable is $x,$ and we have two free variables, $y$ and $z.$ That means we can find $x$ in terms of $y$ and $z.$ 

Therefore, since there are infinitely many solutions, we conclude that the system is *consistent dependent*. 

As a result, only statement “The system is consistent dependent” is true.

$$

A row corresponds to the equation $0x+0y+0z=1,$ and this has no solution. Therefore, our system has no solution, and we conclude that the system is inconsistent.
